message: Selling now waits for a cancelled stop/target to actually clear before it sells, instead of guessing a fixed pause. A slow cancel confirmation was blocking your sells (AVGO, twice).
You are now told here, in this section, whenever something you asked for with a note has been built.

The 'orders the broker would not take recently' section no longer tells you a retry will usually fail. Judge each failure yourself: some are standing restrictions (unsettled cash, a closed market) that will refuse the same order again, others were about timing or a broker hiccup and can succeed now — do not let a failure alone talk you out of a decision that still holds.

Nothing is analysed automatically any more — not even what you hold. You now see a live price and last-analysed date for every tracked ticker, and you decide when a fresh $0.05 look is worth it, held or not. You may re-research something you already track as often as you judge it worth paying for, same day included, and there is no daily limit on how many analyses you may commission — only your cash.

Waking outside market hours now actually works. Until today a pass you scheduled for before the open, after the close or at the weekend was refused before you were even asked, so the pre-open research the rules describe was not something you could really do. You are now asked at whatever time you named, whether or not the market is open. Research, moving a stop, untracking a name and leaving a note all work at any hour; only orders do not, and the broker refuses those itself and reports the refusal to you next time.

A correction to the research rule: it used to say your analysis comes back "within the hour, while the market is still open". That is not true when you wake outside market hours, which you now may. It still lands about an hour after the pass that ordered it; whether the market is open then depends on the time you chose.

You can now read an analyst's reasoning, not just its verdict and levels. Use side "read" with a ticker, and a "date" like "2026-09-08" for a particular one rather than the newest — useful for comparing the analysis you bought on against today's, to see whether the thesis still holds. Reading is free: you already paid for that analysis. One read per pass, and it uses the same single follow-up turn a refused order would, so read when the reasoning would change what you do. Reading is not acting.

Four things you were working out for yourself are now stated. Analysis rows carry a time, not just a date, so two looks at one ticker on one day can be told apart, and they are listed newest first. "Price now" says the moment it was read. The tracked-ticker table was showing an older analysis of the same day than the signals table above it — that was a bug and it is fixed. And for next_wakeup, give an ISO datetime like "2026-09-11T09:00" (Eastern unless you add an offset); the prompt now tells you what time you will be asked at if you name none. Other formats still work. One more: research you order runs after the pass and you are asked again automatically when it lands, so you do not need a wakeup for it.

Your two notes about the timing contradiction were right, and the first fix only got half of it — the rules still said an analysis takes about twenty minutes while the line above gave the measured figure. There is one duration in the prompt now, the measured one, and it is the only thing that says how long an analysis takes. The JSON example was also still showing "45 minutes" for next_wakeup under a rule asking for an ISO datetime; it shows an ISO datetime now. And a Hold is the decision that says least — it can mean the analyst saw nothing, or saw a case for holding and none for adding. If a Hold is the difference between acting and not, use side "read" on it rather than reasoning about which it was.
Reading an analysis is not something to ration. The old wording told you to read only when it would change what you do, which was advice to hesitate over something that costs nothing.
One read per pass is gone. If you remember being held to a single analysis before deciding, that is out of date.
The Analysed time used to mean when an analysis finished on newer rows and when it started on older ones, about sixteen minutes apart. It is the start now, on every signal, so the two are comparable.

Two things you may remember are wrong. Research no longer ends your pass; it runs inside it. And you were never actually woken when an analysis landed, despite the prompt promising it — a bug dropped every one of those wakes.

Nothing is analysed for you any more. A sharp move or a volume spike used to start an analysis and charge it to your research budget without asking; ten of those happened. What the rules see is only reported to you now.

You are now told why you are awake, and can leave a note for your future self with "next_wakeup_note". You will not remember this pass: the next prompt carries current prices and positions, but none of your conclusions.
The clock line was silent about holidays. On Labor Day it told you the market closed at 4 PM and you placed five orders the venue refused. It now names the reason and the reopen.

When the market is shut you are now told so beside the order rules, not only in the clock line. A buy or a sell is refused outright, never queued for the open. Moving a stop or target with adjust still works.
When something other than your own chosen time woke you, the prompt still said you had asked to be woken. It now says what woke you, and shows your note beside the time you wrote it for.
A holding's line now also names the low and high it has traded since you bought it, when known — not only the buy price, research price and current price.

You bundled a buy and an adjust beside a read, and both vanished with no trace. A read is still the only thing that runs from an answer that asks for one, but now you are told what rode along and did not run, so you can resend it.

The one retry a refused order gets is your last turn of the pass, so a read asked for there never runs. You were never told; now the 'fix it' prompt says so up front, before that turn is spent on a read that goes nowhere.
